claim: A hardware security module (HSM) is a computing device that processes cryptographic operations and provides secure storage for cryptographic keys; AWS CloudHSM gives you complete control over high availability HSMs in the AWS Cloud.
question: What is AWS CloudHSM, and what is an HSM?

evidence.quote: A hardware security module (HSM) is a computing device that processes cryptographic operations and provides secure storage for cryptographic keys.

claim: With CloudHSM you receive single-tenant access to each HSM: underlying hardware may be shared with other customers, but the HSM is accessible only to you.
question: Are CloudHSM HSMs shared with other AWS customers?

evidence.quote: As part of the service you receive single-tenant access to the HSM. Underlying hardware may be shared with other customers, but the HSM is accessible only to you.

claim: Amazon has no access to your CloudHSM keys or credentials and has no way to recover your keys if you lose your HSM credentials.
question: Can AWS recover your CloudHSM keys if you lose your HSM credentials?

values.display: has no way to recover your keys
does not have access to your keys

evidence.quote: Amazon does not have access to your keys or credentials and therefore has no way to recover your keys if you lose your credentials.

claim: AWS cannot perform operations on your HSMs: it cannot view or modify your users or keys or perform cryptographic operations with those keys; it uses only the limited appliance user to clone and synchronize HSMs.
question: What can AWS do on your CloudHSM HSMs?

values.display: cannot view or modify your users or keys

evidence.quote: AWS cannot view or modify your users or keys and cannot perform any cryptographic operations using those keys.
The appliance user (AU) can perform cloning and synchronization operations on your cluster's HSMs.

claim: Access to resources inside a CloudHSM cluster uses HSM users on the HSMs, not IAM users or IAM policies; IAM controls only creating HSMs through the AWS API.
question: Do IAM policies control who can use keys inside a CloudHSM cluster?

values.display: you use HSM users directly on HSMs

evidence.quote: Unlike most AWS services and resources, you do not use AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) users or IAM policies to access resources within your AWS CloudHSM cluster. Instead, you use HSM users directly on HSMs in your AWS CloudHSM cluster.
IAM users who have the correct credentials can create HSMs by interacting with resources through the AWS API.

claim: HSM user types include admin, who manages users (create, delete, change passwords), and crypto user (CU), who creates, deletes, shares, imports and exports keys and uses them in cryptographic operations.
question: Which HSM user types exist in CloudHSM and what can each do?

values.display: Create, delete, share, import, and export

evidence.quote: In CloudHSM CLI, admin can perform user management operations. For example, they can create and delete users and change user passwords.
Key management – Create, delete, share, import, and export cryptographic keys.

claim: A CloudHSM cluster is a collection of HSMs that CloudHSM keeps in sync: an operation on one HSM is automatically reflected on the others, and keys that fall out of sync are resynchronized automatically.
question: Do HSMs in a CloudHSM cluster synchronize keys?

evidence.quote: A cluster is a collection of individual HSMs that AWS CloudHSM keeps in sync. When you perform a task or operation on one HSM in a cluster, the other HSMs in that cluster are automatically kept up to date.
If the keys on HSMs in a cluster fall out of synchronization, AWS CloudHSM automatically resynchronizes them.

claim: Unlike keys, HSM users and policies are not automatically resynchronized across the cluster; the CloudHSM CLI makes a best-effort synchronization and you may need to resolve inconsistencies manually.
question: Are HSM users synchronized across a CloudHSM cluster like keys are?

evidence.quote: This automatic resynchronization applies only to keys. Users and policies (such as mTLS settings) are not automatically resynchronized.

claim: HSMs in different Availability Zones give automatic high availability, and AWS recommends a minimum of two HSMs in each cluster, each in a different Availability Zone of the Region; a cluster with more than one HSM is load balanced automatically.
question: How is high availability achieved for CloudHSM?

values.display: a minimum of two HSMs in each cluster

evidence.quote: When you create the HSMs in different AWS Availability Zones, you automatically get high availability.
We recommend that you have a minimum of two HSMs in each cluster, with each HSM in different Availability Zones within an AWS Region.
When you create an AWS CloudHSM cluster with more than one HSM, you automatically get load balancing.

claim: AWS strongly recommends at least two HSMs in two different Availability Zones for any production workload, and at least three HSMs in at least two AZs for mission-critical workloads.
question: How many HSMs should a production CloudHSM cluster have?

evidence.quote: AWS strongly recommends that you use at least two HSMs in two different Availability Zones for any production workload. For mission-critical workloads, we recommend at least three HSMs in at least two separate AZs.

claim: A CloudHSM cluster with a single HSM can lose keys created since the most recent daily backup if the HSM fails; clusters with two or more HSMs, ideally in separate AZs, do not lose keys when a single HSM fails.
question: Could you lose keys if a single CloudHSM HSM fails?

evidence.quote: If your AWS CloudHSM Cluster only has a single HSM, yes it is possible to lose keys that were created since the most recent daily backup. AWS CloudHSM Clusters with two or more HSMs, ideally in separate Availability Zones, will not lose keys if a single HSM fails.

claim: For applications that need durability of newly generated keys, AWS recommends at least three HSMs spread across different Availability Zones, and spreading HSMs across as many AZs as possible.
question: What are the CloudHSM best practices for cluster size and AZ spread?

values.display: across as many Availability Zones as possible

evidence.quote: For applications that require durability of newly generated keys, we recommend having at least three HSMs spread across different Availability Zones in a region.
AWS recommends that you spread your HSMs across as many Availability Zones as possible.

claim: When you create an HSM, CloudHSM puts an elastic network interface in your subnet as the interface to the HSM; the HSM itself resides in a separate VPC in an AWS account owned by CloudHSM.
question: Where does a CloudHSM HSM live relative to your VPC?

evidence.quote: When you create an HSM, AWS CloudHSM puts an elastic network interface (ENI) in the specified subnet in your AWS account. The elastic network interface is the interface for interacting with the HSM. The HSM resides in a separate VPC in an AWS account that is owned by AWS CloudHSM.

claim: The application need not be in the same VPC as the CloudHSM cluster, but the server running the application and HSM client must have network reachability to all HSMs, for example through VPC peering, VPN or Direct Connect.
question: Must the application be in the same VPC as the CloudHSM cluster?

values.display: with VPC peering, with a VPN connection

evidence.quote: No, but the server or instance on which your application and the HSM client are running must have network (IP) reachability to all HSMs in the cluster.

You can establish network connectivity from your application to the HSM in many ways, including operating your application in the same VPC, with VPC peering, with a VPN connection, or with Direct Connect.

claim: CloudHSM makes periodic backups of the cluster's users, keys and policies; the HSM encrypts all data before sending it, the data never leaves the HSM in plaintext, and AWS cannot decrypt the backups.
question: Are CloudHSM backups encrypted, and can AWS read them?

values.display: backups cannot be decrypted by AWS
never leaves the HSM in plaintext form

evidence.quote: AWS CloudHSM makes periodic backups of the users, keys, and policies in the cluster.

When AWS CloudHSM makes a backup from the HSM, the HSM encrypts all of its data before sending it to AWS CloudHSM. The data never leaves the HSM in plaintext form. Additionally, backups cannot be decrypted by AWS because AWS doesn’t have access to key used to decrypt the backups.

claim: AWS takes automatic encrypted backups of a CloudHSM cluster daily and on lifecycle events; for the 24-hour period between backups you alone are responsible for the durability of key material created or imported in the cluster.
question: Who is responsible for key durability in CloudHSM?

values.display: you are solely responsible for the durability

evidence.quote: AWS takes automatic encrypted backups of your CloudHSM Cluster on a daily basis.

AWS takes additional backups when cluster lifecycle events occur (such as adding or removing an HSM).For the 24-hour period between backups, you are solely responsible for the durability of key material created or imported to your cluster.

claim: You can copy CloudHSM cluster backups to other Regions for cross-Region resilience, global workloads and disaster recovery; a cluster built from the copy is not linked to the original and is managed independently, and backups cannot be copied between partitions.
question: Can CloudHSM backups be copied to another Region for disaster recovery?

values.display: cannot be copied between AWS partitions

evidence.quote: You can copy AWS CloudHSM cluster backups across Regions for many reasons, including cross-region resilience, global workloads, and disaster recovery.
The original cluster and the cluster that may be built from a backup in the destination region are not linked. You must manage each of these clusters independently.
Backups cannot be copied between AWS partitions.

claim: Customers whose public key infrastructure uses PKCS #11, Java Cryptographic Extension (JCE), Cryptography API: Next Generation (CNG) or Key Storage Provider (KSP) can migrate to CloudHSM with fewer application changes.
question: Which standard interfaces does CloudHSM support?

evidence.quote: Customers migrating public key infrastructure that use Public Key Cryptography Standards #11 (PKCS #11), Java Cryptographic Extension (JCE), Cryptography API: Next Generation (CNG), or Key Storage Provider (KSP) can migrate to AWS CloudHSM with fewer changes to their application.

claim: Named CloudHSM use cases include offloading SSL/TLS processing for web servers, transparent data encryption (TDE) such as Oracle TDE, managing the private keys of an issuing certificate authority, signing and verifying documents, and regulatory compliance.
question: What are the named use cases for AWS CloudHSM?

values.display: storing the TDE master encryption key

evidence.quote: This process involves a lot of computation for web servers, but you can reduce computational burden while providing extra security by offloading some of this to your AWS CloudHSM cluster.
You can achieve greater security by storing the TDE master encryption key in HSMs in your AWS CloudHSM.
You can store such private keys in your AWS CloudHSM cluster and then use your HSMs to perform cryptographic signing operations.

claim: CloudHSM does not directly support Amazon RDS Oracle TDE; use AWS KMS with a custom key store to protect RDS data with keys generated and stored in your CloudHSM cluster.
question: Can CloudHSM be used directly for Amazon RDS Oracle TDE?

evidence.quote: Not directly. You should use AWS Key Management Service with Custom Key Store to secure Amazon RDS data using keys generated and stored in your CloudHSM Cluster.

claim: AWS services do not use CloudHSM directly; to use server-side encryption of services such as EBS, S3 or RDS with CloudHSM keys, you configure a custom key store in AWS KMS.
question: Can AWS services such as S3 use keys in CloudHSM?

values.display: through the KMS custom key store feature
configuring a custom key store in AWS KMS

evidence.quote: AWS services integrate with AWS Key Management Service, which in turn is integrated with AWS CloudHSM through the KMS custom key store feature. If you want to use the server-side encryption offered by many AWS services (such as EBS, S3, or Amazon RDS), you can do so by configuring a custom key store in AWS KMS.

claim: CloudTrail captures all AWS CloudHSM API calls, but it does not include HSM device or access logs; CloudHSM sends HSM audit logs to CloudWatch Logs on your behalf.
question: Where are CloudHSM API calls logged, and where are HSM audit logs?

values.display: sends them to Amazon CloudWatch Logs

evidence.quote: CloudTrail captures all API calls for AWS CloudHSM as events.
AWS CloudTrail does not include any of the HSM device or access logs. These are provided directly to your AWS account via AWS CloudWatch Logs.
AWS CloudHSM collects your HSM audit logs and sends them to Amazon CloudWatch Logs on your behalf.

claim: CloudHSM charges an hourly fee for each hour or partial hour an HSM is provisioned to a cluster; a cluster with no HSMs is not billed, automatic storage of encrypted backups is not billed, and network data transfer is charged separately.
question: What do you pay for with AWS CloudHSM?

evidence.quote: You will be charged an hourly fee for each hour (or partial hour) that an HSM is provisioned to an AWS CloudHSM cluster. A cluster with no HSMs in it is not billed, nor are you billed for our automatic storage of encrypted backups.
Note that network data transfers to and from your HSMs are charged separately.

claim: Because the CloudHSM data plane is end-to-end encrypted and not visible to AWS, you control your own user management, and the trade-off is more responsibility than with a managed AWS service.
question: What is the trade-off of using CloudHSM instead of a managed service?

evidence.quote: Because your data plane is end-to-end (E2E) encrypted and not visible to AWS, you control your own user management (outside of IAM roles). The trade off for this control is you have more responsibility than if you used a managed AWS service.

claim: If you want a managed service for creating and controlling encryption keys but do not want to operate your own HSMs, AWS suggests AWS KMS; for payment HSMs and keys, AWS Payment Cryptography.
question: When should you choose AWS KMS instead of CloudHSM?

evidence.quote: If you want a managed service for creating and controlling your encryption keys but you don't want or need to operate your own HSMs, consider using AWS Key Management Service.
If you are looking for an elastic service that manages payment HSMs and keys for payment processing applications in the cloud, consider using AWS Payment Cryptography.
